newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ROBSON SAYS BARCELONA BOARD STILL BEHIND HIM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBSON SAYS BARCELONA BOARD STILL BEHIND HIM.

text.p: Beleaguered Barcelona coach Bobby Robson believes that he and his staff still have the backing of the club's board.
"The board continues to think the same and keeps supporting us," said Robson.
The former England manager, had a five-hour meeting with club officials on Monday night in the wake of Barcelona's 2-0 league defeat by Espanyol.
A week earlier he had been promised the board's support, even if they lost to arch rivals Real Madrid in the Spanish Cup. Barcelona won the fourth round tie 4-3 on aggregate.
But defeat by Espanyol in Sunday's Catalan derby left Barcelona eight points behind first division leaders Real.
While Robson remains convinced his job is not under immediate threat, the Spanish media believe his days are numbered.
"Robson is sentenced," read a headline in Barcelona daily El Mundo Deportivo on Tuesday.
Several papers suggest Robson was offered the chance to resign during Monday's meeting and point to Ajax coach Louis Van Gaal as the most likely replacement.
"I'm aware that a scapegoat is being sought and I'm not frightened to be it," Robson said.
The name of former Atletico Madrid manager Tomislav Ivic has also been mentioned. Robson took over from Ivic at Portuguese club Oporto in January 1994.

Club president Jose Luis Nunez -- who earned the wrath of a large section of Barcelona fans for firing Robson's predecessor Johan Cruyff last May -- is understood to be anxious not to have to sack another coach.
A more dignified exit within Barcelona's enormous junior and reserve team structure could have been lined up for Robson.
